newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's programme reflects education priority.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's programme reflects education priority.

text.p: The first legislative programme of the new Labour government will contain three education bills, underscoring Prime Minister Tony Blair's commitment to make education his number one priority, officials said on Wednesday.
They said the Queen's speech next Wednesday, outlining the government's work for the 18-month parliamentary session, would also include measures on health and law and order.
There will be more than a dozen bills in all.
One will pave the way for a parliament in Scotland and an assembly in Wales, while another will set up a commission to fix the level of a national minimum wage.
Legislation will be also be introduced to give effect to Tuesday's announcement that the Bank of England will be given operational repsonsibility for setting interest rates.
The speech will also trail Labour's welfare-to-work programme as well as steps to raise standards in public life.
Officials said there might also be a commitment to set up a London-wide elected authority.
